      "verbatim": "Subsequent more detailed analyses with subdivisions of the amygdala and brainstem showed higher FCs specifically between the BLA on the nonaffected side and the midbrain (t[26] = 2.61, uncorrected P = .015) and between the BLA and VTA (t[26] = 2.07, uncorrected P = .048)."

  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "This study investigated functional connectivity (FC) changes in the brains of human patients with thalamic pain and a macaque model of thalamic pain using resting-state fMRI.",
  "what_it_found": "The study found convergent functional connectivity changes in the amygdala and mediodorsal thalamus in both human patients and macaque models of thalamic pain, suggesting these changes are part of the underlying mechanisms of thalamic pain onset.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "The present results suggest that the FC changes in the regions associated with emotion, memory, motivation, and reward are part of the underlying me­ chanisms of thalamic pain onset present in both human patients and model macaques.",
      "topic": "Cross-species convergence"
    },
    {
      "quote": "This cross-species convergence provides new insights into the neurological mechanisms underlying thalamic pain, paving the way for further studies and the development of therapeutic strategies.",
      "topic": "Implications for therapy"
    },
    {
      "quote": "In humans, the FC between the amygdala on the nonaffected side and the brainstem, specifically between the BLA and VTA, significantly in­ creased in the thalamic pain condition.",
      "topic": "Human findings"
    },
    {
      "quote": "A macaque model of thalamic pain mirrored these results with increased FC between the amygdala on the non­ affected side and brainstem, and more specifically be­ tween the BLA and midbrain.",
      "topic": "Macaque findings"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Conversely, a sig­ nificant pain-related increase in FC between the amyg­ dala and MD, which was the most prominent FC change observed in the macaque model of thalamic pain (Fig 7), was also reproduced in human patients.",
      "topic": "Key convergent finding"
    },
    {
      "quote": "First, the findings from this study may encompass not only painrelated phenomena but also those associated with stroke lesions.",
      "topic": "Study limitations"
    }
  ]
}
